context: Given after plan 218 Task 6's first sitting of gate M-2 (paid run stopped). The decision was given in conversation; the owner's verbatim words were not captured in the repository, so `text` is the wording recorded in plan 218.1 and the commits d893b07f, 2202efb7 and b61c57aa.
text: Remove beam-1m and longmemeval-m from every memory-model gate. They measure question answering over imported chat logs, not the work Prism's memory does: keeping a coding agent's progress across compaction. At about 1M tokens a question they cannot reach a sample size that decides anything (gate M-1: 2 questions per cell; gate M-2: 4).
Prefer external benchmarks over self-designed ones; a test we design is likely biased.

Keep cost and time small at this stage: one lean Compact-Bench screen (retention on 30 sessions, outcome on 22 repair tasks), OpenCode Go only, about $6-10 and half a day of runs; defer the second model, held-out partitions, long-term memory suites and the full gate A.
Claude Code is not used for any benchmark call: its system prompt would be part of what is measured.
The continuation agent is minimax-m3.1-flash on OpenCode Go's native Messages route.
